title: Folders to check
help: One folder per line, from the project root. Empty, the config keeps the folders it names.

title: Folders to leave out
help: One folder per line, never read or reported, such as generated code. This list is what the config leaves out.

title: Rules judged at once
help: How many detectors the check runs side by side. More finish sooner but use more cores and memory.

title: PHP
help: Enables PHP sin detection

title: Vue
help: Enables Vue sin detection

title: TypeScript
help: Enables TypeScript sin detection

title: Python
help: Enables Python sin detection

title: C#
help: Enables C# sin detection

title: BlankStringDefault
help: `string $x = ''` standing in for absence — then asked `$x === ''`

title: BlankStringOnTheWire
help: A `string` field sent over the wire whose TypeScript reader has to check `=== ''` to mean "missing" — only that reader knows the blank stands for absence.

title: CancelledCoalesce
help: `??` cancelled by the comparison it sits in — `($x ?? '') !== ''`

title: ConditionalArraySpread
help: An array built by spreading a conditional element — `...($x ? ['k' => $x] : [])` or `array_merge($base, $cond ? [...] : [])` — a ternary-and-empty-array trick that really just means "include this when the value is present."

title: DeNulledFinder
help: A finder that returns `null` for both "missing" and "broken" instead of throwing — the kind of `?T` finder whose callers all end up de-nulling it.

title: ErasedNullObject
help: A blank-rendering Null Object written into a `string` slot — coerced back to `''`

title: NullableCallback
help: Nullable callback normalised in the body instead of a Null Object default

title: OptionAsNullable
help: `Option<T>` used as if it were nullable — `?Option`, `Option | null`, `unwrapOr(null)`

title: FlagArgument
help: a method whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — or on whether a nullable one was given — two methods sharing one name

title: MemberAfterMethod
help: A trait use, constant, property, property hook, or enum case declared below a method — so the reader only meets that state after seeing the behaviour that uses it.

title: MemberOutOfOrder
help: A declaration in the head of a class that arrives after something belonging below it — a constant under a property, a public field under a private one, a hook above the fields it reads

title: ConcurrentSubclass
help: Class `extends Concurrent` instead of composing `Concurrent<self>`

title: NamespaceCycle
help: two namespaces that reference each other — neither can be read, tested or moved alone

title: NamespaceDependency
help: a declared layer references a layer it may not use (the arrow points back up)

title: ArchaeologyComment
help: History/archaeology comments ("formerly / used to be / refactored / no longer an X / was extracted")

title: BloatedDocblock
help: Multi-paragraph class docblock (class too big)

title: CeremonyDocblock
help: Docblock that only restates the typed signature (`@param Type $x`, no description)

title: DanglingDocReference
help: A docblock `{@see}`/`{@link}` cross-references a FIRST-PARTY class that does not exist in the codebase — documentation pointing at a name that was renamed or removed, never at what the code actually is

title: InlineDocblock
help: A docblock whose delimiter shares a line with its text — a one-liner, or a block that opens or closes next to content

title: NegativeSpaceComment
help: A comment defending the code against a strawman ("not random", "no magic", "not a coincidence", "not dead code")

title: RestatedComment
help: An inline comment that only spells the statement below it back in prose ("// save the order" over `$this->orders->save($order)`)

title: StackedDocblock
help: Two or more docblocks stacked on one declaration — PHP reads only the last, so the ones above it are documentation nobody sees

title: ConstClassEnum
help: A class of 2+ scalar `const`s and nothing else — a closed set hand-rolled as constants instead of a native enum

title: EnumCaseOrChain
help: `$x === Enum::A || $x === Enum::B` — a hand-rolled case-group test

title: EnumValueMatch
help: A `match`/`switch` over an enum's `->value` at the call site — logic that belongs on the enum but lives elsewhere instead.

title: InArrayMirrorsEnum
help: `in_array($x, [literals])` whose literals mirror an existing enum's cases

title: MatchDefaultReturnsNull
help: `match` `default` that returns `null`/`false`/`[]` (or has no body) instead of throwing

title: SideTableTrait
help: An enum holding a trait of some of its cases as a constant list of those cases, instead of as something each case answers for itself.

title: StringMatchMirrorsEnum
help: `match`/`switch` over string/int literals that mirror an existing backed enum's case values

title: UnnamedVocabularyLiteral
help: A raw string in an argument the codebase elsewhere fills from a named vocabulary — `expect('{')` beside `expect(Token::COLON)`, where `Token::BRACE_OPEN` already names it

title: GenericException
help: `throw new <bare SPL>` (RuntimeException/LogicException/…) instead of a named type

title: MessageAtThrow
help: Message string built at the throw site (no domain values / named factory)

title: RethrownUnchanged
help: a `catch` whose whole body is `throw $e;` — the clause catches the failure, adds nothing to it and hands it back on, which is what writing no clause does

title: SwallowCatch
help: `catch` whose only effect is `return null/false/[]`; empty catch (silent swallow)

title: WrappingWithoutCause
help: Wrapping a caught exception without passing it as `previous`/cause

title: ConstructorSideEffect
help: A constructor that performs a side effect on a collaborator and throws away the result, so simply creating the object changes something outside it.

title: DivergentTwin
help: Two functions do the same job, but one of them skips a step the other takes — usually a fix made in one copy and forgotten in the other.

title: DuplicateFunction
help: Copy-pasted code — two+ functions with an identical AST (formatting/comments aside)

title: ManufacturedFakeFill
help: `?? <empty literal>` filling a required slot (manufactured fake)

title: MutableStaticState
help: A write to a static property — really a global variable with a namespace attached — where whichever write happens last wins, so the order code runs in changes the result.

title: NearDuplicateFunction
help: Redundant methods — two+ functions with the same SHAPE differing only in names/literals (type-2 clone)

title: UnreadCollaborator
help: a collaborator promoted into a private field by the constructor and never read anywhere in the class — the class asks for something it does not use, and only a search of the whole type says so

title: CoalescedLoopSubject
help: `foreach ($x[$k] ?? [] as …)` — the absence check buried in the loop header instead of stated as a guard

title: DeepNesting
help: `if` nested 3-deep (a pyramid — hoist guards / extract)

title: IfElseLadder
help: if/elseif ladder of 4+ branches (should be match/dispatch)

title: InlineThrow
help: `?? throw` fed into a call or dereferenced on the same line (inline throw mid-expression)

title: LoopInvertedGuard
help: Loop body (multi-statement) wrapped in an `if` instead of `continue` guard

title: NestedTernary
help: Nested/chained ternary `$a ? $b : ($c ? $d : $e)` (hidden control flow)

title: NonCountingFor
help: A `for` loop that looks like it's counting, but its step actually assigns the next item instead of incrementing a counter.

title: RedundantElse
help: `else` after an `if` branch that already returns/throws (redundant)

title: ShortCircuitStatement
help: a bare `$a && $b->do();` statement — a short-circuit whose result nothing reads, so the operator is an `if` in disguise

title: TernaryStatement
help: a bare `$cond ? doThis() : doThat();` statement — a ternary whose value nothing reads, so it is choosing an ACTION, not a value

title: UnnamedCondition
help: `if ($order->isPaid() && $customer->trusted && $slot->open)` — three parts over two objects, so the reader works out what the condition MEANS instead of reading it

title: ConfigRead
help: `config('…')` read inside a class

title: ContainerReach
help: `app()`/`resolve()` reach inside a container-resolved class

title: DeadConfigKey
help: A config key nothing reads — dead surface left behind by a deleted feature, which new code may wrongly adopt

title: DeadEventWiring
help: An `Event::listen` on an event class no live code path can fire — a listener chain that dead-ends but reads as live wiring

title: DuplicatedConfigDefault
help: A config key whose default is stated TWICE — once in the config file, again as the reader's inline fallback — two sources of truth that drift silently

title: FacadeCall
help: Laravel facade call (`Cache::`, `Log::`, `Mail::` …)

title: MassUpdateAtCallSite
help: Bare `$model->update([...])` mass-array update at a call site

title: ModelMutationAtCallSite
help: Set-property-then-`save()` at a call site (should be an intention method)

title: OrphanedBinding
help: A container binding whose abstract nothing ever resolves — dead wiring that reads as load-bearing and survives every refactor

title: QueryInLoop
help: a query run inside a loop — one query per turn, so the work grows with the data while the code reads as though it were one call

title: RawRequestInput
help: Raw `->input()/->get()/->query()/->post()` on a Request

title: RequestAccessorRecast
help: Re-coercing a typed request accessor at a call site — `$request->string('id')->toString()` or `(string) $request->string('id')` instead of a named getter on a request class

title: BareStatePredicate
help: A `bool` about the object's own state named as a bare verb — `binds()`, `spins()` — where a question belongs

title: NarratedCommand
help: A command named in the third person — `hides()`, `entersTestMode()` — where a call is an order, not a description of one

title: ConstructorOrchestration
help: A page object fills a public slot imperatively in the constructor (`$this->x = $this->projector->…()`) where a `#[Computed]` property hook would describe it in place

title: InjectedServiceNotHidden
help: A page object injects a service (`#[FromContainer]`, …) into a public property without `#[Hidden]` — it leaks into the generated TypeScript type

title: ManualOutputTransform
help: A `Data` computed slot hand-flattens a value object into a wire array, instead of a `#[WithTransformer]` that owns the serialized shape

title: PageObjectMissingTypeScript
help: A page object travels back in a response but carries no `#[TypeScript]` — the `.vue` page reads it as untyped `any`, so the whole page-prop contract goes unchecked

title: ServiceLocationInPageObject
help: A page object reaches into the container with `app()`/`resolve()` instead of injecting the collaborator via `#[FromContainer]`

title: TransformerWithoutTsType
help: A `#[WithTransformer]` changes a property's wire shape but has no paired `#[TypeScriptType]`/`#[LiteralTypeScriptType]`, so the generated TypeScript keeps the wrong (PHP) type

title: ComputedBooleanArgument
help: A parameter that's just true/false, computed by every caller from the same object it could be given instead.

title: ConvertedArgument
help: A parameter typed as the already-converted form instead of the raw value, so every call site repeats the same conversion before calling it (e.g. `Raises::of(ClassAlias::of($interaction), …)`).

title: DerivedArgument
help: Passing the same object twice — once whole and once broken into a piece (`persist($request, $request->shopId())`), or broken into several pieces at once (`new AgentTurn($r->output(), $r->failed(), $r->errorOutput())`) — when the callee could derive each piece itself from the one object.

title: ParamResolvedFromParam
help: Unpacking the target out of a container parameter — a method takes `(Workflow $workflow, string $nodeId)` and resolves `$workflow->graph->nodeById($nodeId)` itself, when it could just receive the node directly.

title: RepeatedGuard
help: The SAME compound guard condition recurs in ≥2 places — the same check spelled differently (inline reaches vs locals) or reordered still counts, so a copied condition has no name

title: RepeatedNamedCall
help: The same `with`-style (variadic) method is called with the same named argument at 2+ sites, instead of a named helper on the type

title: RepeatedTypeGuard
help: The SAME multi-`instanceof` type-narrowing guard (`$x instanceof A && $x->y instanceof B`) is written verbatim in ≥2 places — a check with no name, copied instead of named

title: NullableRegistryLookup
help: A keyed-store `get()` that returns `null` on a miss (should resolve-or-throw)

title: BoundaryDuplicatedOperation
help: The same domain operation hand-rolled at two DIFFERENT entry boundaries (a console command and an MCP tool, a controller and a command) — one operation with two implementations that drift

title: DanglingRouteName
help: A `route('x')` lookup naming a route no registration mints — a stringly cross-reference that only fails at runtime, as a 500

title: DuplicateRoute
help: Two route registrations of the same verb bind different URLs to the SAME `[Controller, method]` — two names for one handler (invokable single-action controllers, commonly aliased to several canonical URLs, are exempt)

title: DuplicateRouteAction
help: Two route actions in different controllers thinly delegate to the SAME operation (`return $this->exporter->export(...)`) — the same entry point twice

title: RouteDelegatesToController
help: A route action forwards to ANOTHER controller's action (`return $this->otherController->action(...)`) — a redundant entry point onto an operation that already has one

title: AllNullableData
help: All-nullable "god" DTO — every field `?T`/defaulted (type doesn't tell the truth)

title: AllOptionalData
help: Every field of a `Data` object is `T|Optional` — the type promises nothing is ever present; the absence belongs on the CONTAINER field where it's used

title: DataCollectionType
help: A `Data` property is TYPED as `DataCollection` — it should be `array` (or `Collection`) with `#[DataCollectionOf(X)]`; the `DataCollection` type emits malformed TypeScript and skips element-typed hydration

title: DataMethodHintCollision
help: `@method` tag that re-declares a real method (names the concrete factory, not the magic `from`/`collect`)

title: HookMissingComputed
help: A get-only property HOOK on a `Data` class lacks `#[Computed]` — Spatie reads the virtual property as a hydration INPUT, expects it in `::from()`, and crashes or silently drops it

title: ManualHydrationLoop
help: Collections hydrated with `::from()` per item instead of `#[DataCollectionOf]` + `::collect()`

title: ManualInputCast
help: A `Data` value-object property is hand-built at every construction site, instead of a `#[WithCast]` / `Castable` that owns the hydration once

title: NestedTypeMissingTypeScript
help: A `#[TypeScript]` Data has a property typed as a nested `Data` class that itself lacks `#[TypeScript]` — the transformer emits it as `undefined`, a silent hole in the generated type (a nested enum is fine; the enum collector auto-generates it)

title: NewDataObject
help: `new <Data subclass>` instead of `::from()` / a `fromX()` factory

title: NonFinalData
help: Data class not `final` / props not `readonly` promoted

title: NullToOptionalMap
help: A producer hand-maps null→`new Optional` — `$x === null ? new Optional : Foo::from($x)` or `expr() ?? new Optional` — instead of one named factory (Spatie's `optional()` maps null→null, the opposite of what a `T|Optional` slot needs)

title: NullableWireObject
help: A nested object on a `#[TypeScript]` Data is typed `T | null` — it ships `null` on the wire where `T | Optional` would OMIT it (what the frontend's `x?.` reads for "absent")

title: PreferOptionalCreate
help: A raw `new Optional` is constructed in a runtime expression where Spatie's built-in `Optional::create()` factory reads clearer

title: DataToArrayRoundtrip
help: A `X::from(...)->toArray()` sits in a `::from` slot typed `X` that re-hydrates it — build → array → build

title: DerivedCollectionCast
help: A `#[DataCollectionOf]` is filled by mapping a factory over inputs at the call site, where a `#[WithCast]` should own the derivation

title: HandKeyRemap
help: A `::from([...])` mechanically renames `$src['snake_key']` → `camelKey` by hand, instead of a class-level `#[MapInputName]`

title: RedundantEnumUnwrap
help: An enum is unwrapped to `->value` at a hydration site (`'status' => $order->status->value`) where the property is typed as that enum — Spatie re-casts the scalar straight back to the enum

title: RedundantNativeCast
help: An enum / date is constructed at a hydration site (`Enum::from($x)`, `new DateTime($x)`) where the property auto-casts the raw scalar

title: RedundantNestedFrom
help: A nested `X::from([...])` fills a slot the parent `::from` already auto-hydrates from the array

title: FeatureEnvy
help: Exiled behaviour / feature envy — a method operating on ONE other owned object's internals that belongs ON that object

title: KeyedLookupEnvy
help: Indirect feature envy — a method that uses an owned object's IDENTITY as a key to look up a fact about it through a collaborator

title: TrainWreck
help: `$order->customer()->address()->city()` — a chain crossing three of the project's own types, so a change three objects away reaches this caller

title: TypeSwitch
help: two or more `instanceof` tests on the same subject deciding different branches — asking a value what it IS instead of telling it what to do

title: AssembledTemplate
help: A multi-line template assembled as an array of line fragments and joined with a newline — the output is unreadable in the source that emits it

title: FilledParameter
help: a `void` method that writes a property of an object it was handed, whose caller then reads what it handed over — the signature says the object goes in and nothing says it comes out changed

title: ImpossibleGuard
help: `if ($order === null)` where `$order` is typed `Order`, with no `?` — one of the two is wrong, and both are worth knowing

title: MaskedInvariant
help: Masked invariant — an own field read as `?->… ?? <fake literal>`, even though the very operation sets that field first, so the fallback only ever answers an impossible "not set yet".

title: PhantomNullable
help: Phantom nullable — a field typed `?T` (promoted param or declared property, any class) whose value, traced through the whole program, is always read as present and NEVER guarded, so the null never happens

title: PlaceholderFilledData
help: A required non-nullable `string` slot handed `''` — the type promises a value that is always there and the caller has none

title: RedundantArrowReturnType
help: An arrow function whose return type only repeats what its one expression provably yields — `fn (): string => $this->name` on a `string` property

title: ScratchStateRestore
help: Scratch state on `$this` — a method that saves one of its own fields to a local and restores it (`$prev = $this->scope; … $this->scope = $prev`), the field really a per-call input

title: UselessPropertyHook
help: A `get` hook that reads nothing from `$this` — a stored property wearing computed syntax

title: ArrayBag
help: String-indexing (`$arr['key']`) a structured array param instead of giving it a name — the type was never defined.

title: ArrayReturnBag
help: Returning a multi-field string-keyed array literal (a bag that should be a value object)

title: CoupledFields
help: A class's own fields always change and get checked together — one concept split across several fields — and should be folded into a single value object.

title: DataClump
help: The same 3+ scalar params threaded through 2+ classes (a recurring data clump → one object)

title: FlatFieldCluster
help: A `#[TypeScript]` `Data` class spreads a value object it already models flat across sibling scalar fields sharing a camelCase prefix (`wireType` + `wireLabel`) instead of nesting the existing `Wire{type, label}`.

title: HandRolledWither
help: A wither method rebuilds the whole object by re-listing every constructor field, so adding a new field means updating every wither in the class.

title: MutableValueObject
help: A value type that mutates its own field after construction, so two things holding what should be the same value can end up different — one changes without the other knowing.

title: PositionalTupleReturn
help: Returning a positional TUPLE — `return [$node, $key, $inputs, $outputs]` — bundling independent values as a keyless list the caller destructures by position

title: RawDecodedArrayReturn
help: Returning a raw decoded boundary array (`json_decode(...)`) untyped

title: BlankStringDefault
help: a `string` parameter or property defaulted to `""` and then checked with `== ""` or `string.IsNullOrEmpty` — the blank is being used to mean "missing"

title: CancelledCoalesce
help: a `??` fallback compared against the same value it falls back to — `(name ?? "") != ""` — so "missing" and "empty" end up in one branch without saying so

title: DeNulledFinder
help: a finder returning a nullable object whose every caller asserts it is there — `Find(id)!`, `Find(id) ?? throw …` — a miss the finder should have refused itself

title: InventedDefault
help: `F(x ?? "")` — an empty string, `0` or `false` invented to fill an argument, or answered by a lookup helper on a miss, a stand-in the callee cannot tell from real data

title: NullForgiven
help: The null-forgiving `!` on a value declared nullable — the compiler told the caller it may be null, and `!` silences it instead of deciding

title: FlagArgument
help: a method whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — `if (compact) … else …` — two methods sharing one name

title: MemberAfterMethod
help: a field, constant or stored property declared below a constructor or a method — the type's state hidden among its behaviour

title: MemberOutOfOrder
help: a `const` or `static readonly` value declared below a field or a stored property — the top of the type read in no particular order

title: NamespaceCycle
help: two of the project's namespaces that each use the other — a cycle that makes them one namespace split under two names

title: NamespaceDependency
help: a reference out of a declared layer into a namespace that layer did not declare it may use

title: ArchaeologyComment
help: a comment that tells the code's past — `// formerly lived in CheckoutService`, `// refactored to use the cache` — describing a version nobody is reading

title: BloatedDocblock
help: a type whose doc comment runs to two or more paragraphs — usually a sign the type does too much

title: CeremonyDocblock
help: a doc comment whose every tag is empty or only repeats the signature — `<param name="order">The order.</param>`, an empty `<returns>`

title: DanglingDocReference
help: a `<see cref>` that resolves to nothing from where it is written — a name the project no longer declares, or one spelled so it does not reach it

title: NegativeSpaceComment
help: a comment defending the code against a reading nobody made — `// not magic, just a day`, `// deliberately not sorted` — saying what it is not instead of what it is

title: RestatedComment
help: a comment above a statement whose every word the statement already spells — `// set the total to the order total` over `var total = order.Total;`

title: DuplicateMethod
help: Copy-pasted code — two+ C# methods, accessors or local functions with an identical body, formatting, comments and attributes aside

title: NearDuplicateMethod
help: A near-copy — two+ C# methods, accessors or local functions with one control-flow skeleton that differ only in their local names or the literals they use (a key, a route, a message)

title: ConstClassEnum
help: a class that holds nothing but `const` strings or numbers — a closed set of values written as constants instead of an `enum`

title: EnumCaseOrChain
help: `s == Status.Paid || s == Status.Refunded` (or `s is Status.Paid or Status.Refunded`) — a group of enum cases tested by hand at the call site

title: InArrayMirrorsEnum
help: `new[] { "paid", "refunded" }.Contains(status)` or `status is "paid" or "refunded"` — a list of strings that repeats the members of an enum the code already has

title: MatchDefaultReturnsNull
help: a `switch` that names every member of an enum, then answers `null`, `default` or `false` in its `_` arm — the one value that arm can see is a bug, and it is answered as if it were fine

title: StringMirrorsEnum
help: A `switch` or an `if` ladder dispatching on strings that are the names of an enum the codebase already declares — the enum, written out again as text

title: UnnamedVocabularyLiteral
help: a raw string handed to a parameter the codebase elsewhere fills from a named constant — `Expect("{")` beside `Expect(Token.Colon)`, where `Token.BraceOpen` already names it

title: GenericThrow
help: `throw new Exception/InvalidOperationException("…")` — a failure that names nothing, described in prose at the throw site

title: RethrownUnchanged
help: a `catch` whose whole body is `throw;` or `throw error;` — the clause catches the failure, adds nothing to it and hands it back on, which is what writing no clause does

title: SwallowedException
help: A bare `catch` or `catch (Exception)` whose body is empty, continues, or returns nothing — every failure, expected or not, made to vanish

title: WrappingWithoutCause
help: a `catch` that throws a new exception without passing the caught one as its inner exception, so the original stack trace is lost

title: BlockedAwait
help: `.Result`, `.Wait()` or `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` on a task — the thread it blocks is the one the work needed back, so it deadlocks under load and nowhere else

title: ConstructorSideEffect
help: a constructor that calls a method on something it was handed and ignores the result — just creating the object changes something outside it

title: MutableStaticState
help: a `static` field that methods write to — state no instance owns, changed by whichever code ran last

title: UnreadCollaborator
help: a private readonly field, or a primary constructor parameter, that nothing in the type reads — the type asks for something it does not use

title: CoalescedLoopSubject
help: a `foreach` over `items ?? []` (or `Enumerable.Empty<T>()`, or a new empty list) — the check for a missing collection is hidden in the loop header

title: CollectionMutatedWhileIterated
help: a `foreach` that adds to or removes from the very collection it walks — the enumerator reads a collection that moved under it, which throws InvalidOperationException

title: InlineThrow
help: a `?? throw` inside a call's argument or in front of a member call — the check that stops the method is hidden in the middle of the work

title: LoopWrappedInIf
help: A `for`, `foreach` or `while` whose whole body is one `if` (no `else`) around real work — the iteration pushed a level deep behind a condition

title: NestedTernary
help: a `?:` with another `?:` as one of its branches — several decisions packed into one expression

title: NonCountingFor
help: a `for` loop whose step assigns the next item instead of moving a counter — a walk written as a count

title: SubjectLadder
help: An `if`/`else if` chain of four or more rungs that each compare the same subject with a constant — a dispatch written as a ladder.

title: UnnamedCondition
help: `if (order.IsPaid && customer.Trusted && slot.IsOpen)` — three parts over two objects, so the reader works out what the condition MEANS instead of reading it

title: DeepNesting
help: An `if`, loop or `switch` opening a fourth level of choices inside one C# method — an arrow of conditions and loops

title: RedundantElse
help: An `else` after an `if` branch that already left — it ends in `return`, `throw`, `continue` or `break` — indenting the rest of the method for nothing

title: BareStatePredicate
help: a `bool` about the object's own state named as a claim — `Binds()`, `Spins` — where a question belongs

title: ConvertedArgument
help: a scalar parameter its callers keep filling with the same conversion — `ReceiptFor(order.Id.ToString())` call after call — because it asks for the converted form instead of the value

title: DerivedArgument
help: a call that hands over an object and a projection of it — `Persist(request, request.ChannelId)` — or an object in three pieces, where the method could read them itself

title: ParamResolvedFromParam
help: a method that takes a container and a key and first resolves one against the other — `Rename(Workflow workflow, string nodeId)` doing `workflow.Graph.Node(nodeId)` — when it only wanted what the key names

title: RepeatedGuard
help: the same compound condition — `order.Paid && !order.Cancelled` — written at two or more sites, a question with no name

title: RepeatedNamedCall
help: the same `with` copy — `order with { Status = OrderStatus.Shipped }` — written at two or more sites, an operation the record never named

title: RepeatedTypeGuard
help: the same chain of type checks — `node is Invocation call && call.Target is MemberAccess` — written at two or more sites, a shape with no name

title: FeatureEnvy
help: a method that loops another object's collection or writes its members, reaching into it more than into its own state — behaviour exiled from the object it works on

title: SideTableTrait
help: a trait of a type's registered instances kept as a separate collection of their names, rather than as something each instance answers for itself

title: TypeSwitch
help: `shape switch { Circle c => …, Square s => … }` — asking which of your own types a value is, to decide what to do with it

title: AssembledTemplate
help: `string.Join("\n", new[] { "public class X", "{", "}" })` or `sb.AppendLine("…")` line after line — a multi-line text built from line fragments, so its shape cannot be seen in the source

title: FilledParameter
help: a method returning nothing that writes a property of an object it was handed, whose caller then reads what it handed over — the signature says the object goes in and nothing says it comes out changed

title: ImpossibleGuard
help: `if (order == null)` where `order` is typed `Order` and not `Order?` — one of the two is wrong, and both are worth knowing

title: PlaceholderFilledData
help: `new Card(title, "")` — a record's required `string` filled with a blank so the record can be built, hiding a missing value no type check can see

title: ArrayReturnBag
help: a method that returns `new Dictionary<string, object> { ["sku"] = …, ["qty"] = … }` — a record with fixed fields, handed back as a dictionary

title: CoupledFields
help: a type whose own fields always travel together — assembled into one value again and again, null-checked together, or one copying what a sibling field already holds — one concept held as several fields

title: DataClump
help: The same three or more string, number, date or id parameters threaded through methods of two or more types — values that always travel together but have no type of their own.

title: DictionaryBag
help: A string-keyed dictionary or JSON object read by keys written in the source — `row["sku"]`, `json.GetProperty("name")` — a record nobody declared

title: HandedOutCollection
help: a property or method whose whole body returns the type's own `List`, `Dictionary` or `HashSet`, untouched — every caller holds the insides and may add to or take from them without the type knowing

title: MutableValueObject
help: a record that can change after it is built — a `set` accessor, or a method that writes its own state — so two holders of the same value can end up seeing different things

title: PositionalTupleReturn
help: a method that returns `(decimal, decimal, string)` — unnamed values the caller reads by position, where two of the same type can be swapped and nothing notices

title: MirroredServerType
help: A hand-written TypeScript type mirrors a backend `Data` class one-to-one — two sources of truth for one contract that drift the moment the server shape changes

title: CompoundInlineComponent
help: A compound primitive (`Dialog`/`Card`/`Sheet`/`Tabs`…) assembled inline with a substantial body — extract it into its own named component.

title: DeepDataReach
help: A group of elements in a sizeable template that all reach deep into the same nested object (≥2 distinct fields) — extract the shared mid-object into a component that takes it as a prop.

title: DeepNested
help: Template markup nested far too deep — extract a subtree as its own component

title: DuplicateElement
help: Identical markup (3+ elements) repeated 2+ times — within a template or across components — extract one component

title: InlineCaseViews
help: A dispatch whose cases each render a whole view inline — one component doing a job per case

title: NearDuplicateElement
help: Markup with one skeleton repeated 2+ times — the same tags, attributes and nesting binding different data — within a template, across components, or as two components' whole templates

title: OversizedComponent
help: A component whose template renders more elements than the project's declared budget — one component doing several jobs

title: PropDrilling
help: A prop forwarded through a chain of 2+ components, none of which read it — passed down through components that only pass it further.

title: PropMutation
help: A prop is written to — `v-model` bound to it, or `@event="prop = …"` — but props are read-only (a build error or a silent no-op).

title: ControlFlowOnElement
help: `v-if`/`v-for`/`v-else`/`v-else-if` on an HTML/component tag instead of a `<template>`

title: IndexAsKey
help: `:key` bound to the `v-for` index — a positional key corrupts state when the list reorders or an item is inserted

title: LoopWithCondition
help: `v-for` and `v-if`/`v-else-if` on the same element — the condition is re-evaluated every iteration.

title: SwitchCase
help: A `v-if`/`v-else-if` chain re-testing the same subject (should be `<SwitchCase :value>`)

title: BlankStringDefault
help: `x: str = ""` standing in for absence — then asked `x == ""`, `not x` or `if x:` in its own scope

title: CancelledFallback
help: `(x or "") != ""` — a value defaulted to a blank only to be compared against that same blank, so a missing value and an empty one are treated the same without saying so.

title: ConditionalSpread
help: `**({"k": v} if v else {})` / `*([x] if x else [])` — an entry is spread in only when present, using a conditional that turns absence into an empty collection.

title: InventedDefault
help: `f(x or "")` — an empty string, `0` or `False` invented to fill an argument when the value is missing, a stand-in the callee cannot tell from real data

title: NullableCallback
help: `cb: Callable | None = None` asked `if cb is not None:` / `if cb:` / `cb or …` in the body — a no-op treated as if it might be missing.

title: FlagArgument
help: a function whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — or on whether an optional one was given — two functions sharing one name

title: MemberAfterMethod
help: a constant, class attribute or field declared below a method — the class's state hidden among its behaviour

title: MemberOutOfOrder
help: a constant declared below a field in the head of a class — the inventory read in an ad-hoc order

title: NamespaceCycle
help: two of the project's packages import each other — a cycle that makes them one package split under two names.

title: NamespaceDependency
help: an import out of a declared layer into a package that layer did not declare it may use

title: ArchaeologyComment
help: a comment or docstring narrating the code's history — where it lived, what it replaced, what it no longer is

title: BloatedDocblock
help: a class docstring of two or more paragraphs of prose — an essay that says the class does too much

title: CeremonyDocblock
help: a docstring with no summary whose every entry restates the annotated signature — `order (Order):`, `:rtype: int`

title: DanglingDocReference
help: a Sphinx cross-reference in a docstring (`:class:`shop.cart.Basket``) to a first-party name the codebase no longer declares

title: NegativeSpaceComment
help: a comment or docstring defending the code against a misunderstanding nobody actually had — what it is not, rather than what it is.

title: RestatedComment
help: a `#` comment that only narrates the statement below it — every word of it already spelled by the code

title: DuplicateFunction
help: Copy-pasted code — two+ Python functions or methods with an identical body, formatting, comments and docstrings aside

title: NearDuplicateFunction
help: A near-copy — two+ Python functions or methods with one control-flow skeleton that differ only in their local names or the literals they use (a path, a key, a message)

title: ConstantClassEnum
help: a class that is nothing but `PENDING = "pending"` constants — a closed set of values written out by hand instead of an `Enum`

title: EnumCaseOrChain
help: `s == Status.PENDING or s == Status.LATE` — a group of an enum's members re-derived at the call site instead of named on the enum

title: EnumValueMatch
help: `match status.value: case "paid": …` at a call site — the enum's raw values matched again where the enum could answer

title: InLiteralsMirrorsEnum
help: `x in ("pending", "late")` whose literals are an existing enum's values — a group of its members spelled as raw strings at the call site

title: MatchWildcardReturnsNone
help: a `match` over an enum's members whose `case _:` returns `None` — a member nobody handled answers nothing instead of failing

title: StringMatchMirrorsEnum
help: `match raw: case "pending": …` whose cases are an existing enum's values — dispatching on loose strings the enum already seals

title: UnnamedVocabularyLiteral
help: a raw string handed to a parameter the codebase elsewhere fills from a named constant — `expect("{")` beside `expect(Token.COLON)`, where `Token.BRACE_OPEN` already names it

title: MessageStringRaise
help: `raise Exception/RuntimeError("…")` — a failure that names nothing, described in prose at the raise site

title: RaiseWithoutCause
help: `raise Other(...)` inside an `except` block with no `from` — the failure being handled left as an implicit context, never named as the cause

title: RethrownUnchanged
help: an `except` whose whole body is `raise` or `raise error` — the clause catches the failure, adds nothing to it and hands it back on, which is what writing no clause does

title: SwallowedException
help: A bare `except:` or `except Exception` whose body only passes, continues or returns nothing — every failure, expected or not, made to vanish

title: BlockedAwait
help: `time.sleep`, `requests.get` or `subprocess.run` inside an `async def` — the thread it stops is the event loop, so every coroutine waiting on it stops too

title: ConstructorSideEffect
help: an `__init__` that tells a collaborator to act and throws the answer away — merely building the object has an effect outside it.

title: DivergentTwin
help: two functions do the same job, but one of them skips a step the other takes — usually a fix made in one copy and forgotten in the other.

title: FrozenDefault
help: a parameter defaulted to `datetime.now()`, `uuid4()` or another call that answers differently each time — it runs once when the def is defined, so every call that omits it gets the moment the module was imported

title: MutableDefault
help: a parameter defaulted to a `[]`, `{}` or `set()` — one container, made once, shared by every call that omits it

title: MutableStaticState
help: a `global` written from a function, or a class attribute set from a method — state no instance owns, changed by whoever ran last

title: UnreadCollaborator
help: a collaborator `__init__` keeps as an attribute of its own, `self._mailer = mailer`, that nothing anywhere reads — the class asks for something it does not use

title: DeepNesting
help: An `if`, loop or `match` opening a fourth level of choices inside one Python function — an arrow of conditions and loops

title: CoalescedLoopSubject
help: `for x in d.get(k, [])` / `for x in y or []` over a parameter — whether the caller handed anything over, decided in the loop header instead of stated as a guard

title: CollectionMutatedWhileIterated
help: a loop that appends to, removes from or deletes out of the very collection it walks — the iterator reads a sequence that moved under it, so an element is skipped or it raises

title: ConditionalStatement
help: a bare `a() if x else b()` statement — a conditional expression whose value nothing reads, so it chooses an action, not a value.

title: LoopWrappedInIf
help: A `for` or `while` whose whole body is one `if` (no `else`) around real work — the iteration pushed a level deep behind a condition

title: NestedConditional
help: `a if x else b if y else c` — a conditional expression inside another's branch, a branching decision folded into one line

title: ShortCircuitStatement
help: a bare `a and b()` or `a or b()` statement — an `and`/`or` whose value nothing reads, so the operator is really acting as an `if`.

title: SubjectLadder
help: An `if`/`elif` chain of four or more rungs that each test the same subject for equality with a constant — a dispatch written as a ladder.

title: UnnamedCondition
help: `if settings.auto and not self.said and event.at > self.since:` — three parts over two objects, so the reader works out what the condition MEANS instead of reading it

title: RedundantElse
help: An `else:` after an `if` branch that already left — it ends in `return`, `raise`, `continue` or `break` — indenting the rest of the function for nothing

title: BareStatePredicate
help: a `bool` about the object's own state named as a bare verb — `binds()`, `spins` — where a question belongs

title: NarratedCommand
help: a command named in the third person — `hides()`, `locks_for_night()` — where a call is an order, not a description of one

title: ComputedBooleanArgument
help: a method taking only bools that every caller computes from the same object — the decision re-derived at each call site

title: ConvertedArgument
help: a scalar parameter its callers keep filling with the same conversion — `receipt_for(str(order.id))` call after call — because it asks for the converted form instead of the value

title: DerivedArgument
help: a call that hands over an object and a projection of it — `persist(request, request.channel_id)` — or an object in three pieces, where the function could read them itself

title: ParamResolvedFromParam
help: a function that takes a container and a key and first resolves one against the other — `def rename(workflow, node_id)` doing `workflow.graph.node(node_id)` — when it only wanted what the key names

title: RepeatedGuard
help: the same compound `and` condition recurs in 2+ places — it still counts even when reordered, or read through a local variable — and nobody has named it.

title: RepeatedNamedCall
help: the same `**changes` call is built the same way with the same keyword at 2+ sites — an operation that has no name on the type it belongs to.

title: RepeatedTypeGuard
help: the same multi-`isinstance` narrowing (`isinstance(x, A) and isinstance(x.y, B)`) is written in 2+ places — a check on a shape that nobody has named.

title: NullableRegistryLookup
help: a keyed store handing back `None` for a key it lacks — `return self._handlers.get(kind)` — so every caller decides what a miss means

title: FeatureEnvy
help: a method that loops another object's collection or writes its fields, reaching into it more than into its own state — behaviour exiled from the object it works on

title: KeyedLookupEnvy
help: a method that uses an object's key to fetch a fact about it through a collaborator — `self.registry.get(node.key).reserved` — treating the object as a key into its own data

title: SideTableTrait
help: a trait of a type kept in a collection of its instances' names beside the registry, rather than as a field each instance answers for itself

title: TypeSwitch
help: an `isinstance` ladder over classes the codebase owns — the value is asked what it is so the caller can decide what to do.

title: AssembledTemplate
help: a multi-line string built as a list of line fragments and `"\n".join(...)`-ed, instead of a triple-quoted f-string that shows its output

title: ConstantProperty
help: an `@property` whose body never reads `self` — `return "box"` — a stored value made to look like a computed one.

title: FilledParameter
help: a def returning `None` that writes an attribute of an object it was handed, whose caller then reads what it handed over — the signature says the object goes in and nothing says it comes out changed

title: ImpossibleGuard
help: `if order is None` where `order` is annotated as a class with no `| None` — one of the two is wrong, and both are worth knowing

title: MaskedInvariant
help: a literal answering for the object's own scratch state — `self.period.includes(day) if self.period else False` — where the field is only unset because an operation sets it part-way

title: PhantomNullable
help: a field annotated `X | None` that every read assumes is there and none guards — a `None` the design never has

title: PlaceholderFilledData
help: `Card(title=…, body="")` — a dataclass field required as `str` handed the blank to satisfy the signature, a value the type cannot catch

title: ScratchStateRestore
help: `previous = self.scope … self.scope = previous` — an attribute used as per-call scratch, saved and restored around the call

title: CoupledFields
help: a class whose own fields always travel together — assembled into one value again and again, guarded together, or one copying a sibling field's value — one concept held as several fields.

title: DataClump
help: The same three or more scalar parameters (`street: str, city: str, postcode: str`) threaded through functions in two or more classes or modules — one concept with no type of its own.

title: DictBag
help: A parameter typed as a dict read by string keys — `row["sku"]`, `row.get("quantity")` — a record nobody declared

title: DictReturnBag
help: `return {"total": …, "tax": …}` — a record of several fields handed back as a dict its callers read by string key

title: HandRolledReplace
help: `return Order(self.number, self.lines, self.note, "paid")` in a dataclass — every field re-listed to change one

title: HandedOutCollection
help: a getter whose whole body returns the class's own `list`, `dict` or `set`, untouched — every caller holds the insides and may add to or take from them without the class knowing

title: MutableValueObject
help: a dataclass whose own methods write the fields it was built from after construction — a value that changes under everyone holding it

title: PositionalTupleReturn
help: `return net, vat, currency` — a bundle of different things the caller must unpack by position, where a reordering breaks silently

title: RawDecodedReturn
help: `return json.loads(…)` — decoded text from outside handed on as bare dicts and lists, its shape known to no type

title: DefendedCertainField
help: An `?.` on a field the class declares as always present — a defence against a case the type says cannot happen, so the code doubts something the design already rules out.

title: FalselyOptionalField
help: A field declared optional (`x?: T`, `T | null`) that is initialised where it is declared — it is never absent, and every `?.` and `??` downstream defends a case that cannot happen

title: DuplicateFunction
help: Copy-pasted code — two+ TypeScript functions (a `function`, a method, a `const` arrow; in a `.ts` module or a component's script) with an identical body, formatting and comments aside

title: NearDuplicateFunction
help: A near-copy — two+ TypeScript functions with one control-flow skeleton that differ only in their local names or the literals they use (an endpoint, a key, a label)

title: SideTableTrait
help: a trait of the objects a module registers, kept as a separate collection of their names rather than as a field each object carries
